question: In which year did Smriti Mandhana become the fastest Indian woman to reach 4,000 ODI runs?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian opening batter **Smriti Mandhana** scripted history in **February 2025** by becoming the **fastest Indian woman** to reach the milestone of **4,000 runs** in **One Day International (ODI)** cricket.
 
• She achieved this significant feat during the **third ODI** match of the series against **New Zealand**, held at **Seddon Park** in **Hamilton**.
 
• Mandhana reached the **4,000-run mark** in just her **100th innings**, showcasing her remarkable consistency and scoring rate since her debut.
 
• By achieving this in **100 innings**, she broke the long-standing national record held by the legendary **Mithali Raj**, who had reached the same milestone in **109 innings**.
 
• Globally, she became the **third-fastest woman** to reach **4,000 ODI runs**, trailing only Australia’s **Meg Lanning** (who reached it in **82 innings**) and England’s **Nat Sciver-Brunt** (who reached it in **99 innings**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Smriti Mandhana:**
 
 
• Born on **July 18, 1996**, in **Mumbai, Maharashtra**, she is a prolific **left-handed opening batter** for the **Indian Women’s National Team**.
 
• She made her **ODI debut** in **2013** against **Bangladesh** and her Test debut in **2014** against **England**.
 
• Mandhana has been awarded the **ICC Women’s Cricketer of the Year** (Rachael Heyhoe Flint Award) twice, in **2018** and **2021**, recognizing her as one of the best players in the world.
 
• In domestic franchise cricket, she serves as the **captain** of the **Royal Challengers Bangalore (RCB)** in the **Women’s Premier League (WPL)** and led the team to their maiden title in **2024**.
 
 
 
• **Milestones in Women’s ODIs:**
 
 
• Mandhana is only the **third Indian woman** to aggregate more than **4,000 runs** in the ODI format, joining the elite company of **Mithali Raj** and **Harmanpreet Kaur**.
 
• She also holds the record for being the first Indian to score a **double century** in a **one-day game** (achieved during a domestic **Under-19 tournament** in **2013**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Statistical Comparison:** While **Mithali Raj** remains the highest run-scorer in women’s ODI history with **7,805 runs**, Mandhana’s pace of scoring suggests she is a primary contender to challenge global records in the coming years.
 
• **2025 Context:** The year **2025** is a pivotal year for women’s cricket in **India** as the country prepares for the **ICC Women’s Cricket World Cup**. Mandhana’s form is considered crucial for India's prospects in major international **ICC tournaments**.
 
• **Awards and Honors:** Apart from **ICC** honors, she was conferred with the **Arjuna Award** in **2018** by the **Government of India** for her outstanding achievements in sports.
